title: Operator cheatsheet: SLI corruption detection and metric healing
content:
Purpose
This is a working cheatsheet for oncall operators and observability engineers to detect SLI/metric corruption early, triage, and apply automated or manual metric healing steps. Focus is token-serving and inference SLI signals (latency, error-rate, kv-warmth, throughput).

Audience
- Oncall SREs / operators
- Observability maintainers
- Serving runtime owners

Context / motivation
We see periodic cases where an SLI dashboard shows large regressions but the underlying user impact is not present (false alarms). Root causes range from instrumentation drift, metric-tagging changes, delayed ingestion pipelines, to query explosion causing SLA artifacts. False positives increase toil and hide real issues. This doc groups heuristics, detection patterns, and healing steps to reduce mean time to detect/repair for metric-corruption incidents.

Quick detection recipes (first 5 minutes)
1) Correlation sanity check (1–2 min):
   - Compare SLI spike to external indicators: incident reports, customer tickets, upstream infra alerts.
   - If no external signal, suspect metric integrity.
2) Cross-slice check (2–3 min):
   - Run pre-baked queries comparing global SLI vs per-tenant top-10 tenants and synthetic probes.
   - Example queries (pseudo):
     - global_50p_latency by minute vs top10_tenant_avg_50p_latency
     - synthetic_probe_ttfb_requests / synthetic_probe_count
   - If global shifts but all tenants and probes are flat → metric ingestion issue.
3) Time-shift replay (2 min):
   - Check delayed ingestion: run a 10m time-shifted view (now-30m => now-20m) to detect late-arriving metrics.
4) Tag drift detection (3–5 min):
   - Validate expected tag cardinality for critical labels (model, route, tenant). Sudden drop to <80% of baseline indicates tag-loss.

Common corruption modes and indicators
- Metric duplication / double-counting
  - Symptom: token_count, request_count jump ~2x while traces and infra remain steady.
  - Check: ingestion pipeline logs for duplicate batches; metric-uuid changes in Kafka.
- Tagging loss (label removed at instrumentation)
  - Symptom: per-model heatmaps flatten; global still shows high.
  - Check: metric cardinality, unique tag counts and recent deploys touching client lib or runtime.
- Aggregation pipeline outage (rollup/aggregator down)
  - Symptom: sharp drops in derived signals (qps, p50) with raw event queues increasing.
  - Check: aggregator service health, queue backlog, consumer lag.
- Query/alert mis-evaluation due to query changes
  - Symptom: alerts firing only for certain panels after a metrics rename.
  - Check: alert query diffs, metric renames in PRs.
- Sampling/config flag error (trace/metrics sampling)
  - Symptom: trace-linking disappears while raw metrics persist; or opposite.
  - Check: sampler config rollout, feature-flag recent changes.

Triage checklist (detailed)
- Step A: Validate user impact
  - Slack #incidents / ticket queue / synthetic probe dashboards.
  - Customer-facing telemetry (if available): session recordings, replay logs.
- Step B: Confirm metric health
  - Check ingestion latency distribution and last-seen per metric series.
  - Run cardinality histogram for critical labels.
  - Confirm retention/rollup service metrics (consumer lag, write error rate).
- Step C: Inspect deploys and config changes (last 30 minutes)
  - GitHub PRs merged, infra config, canary rollouts, config flags.
- Step D: Narrow to component
  - Use trace anchors: pick a sample request id and follow spans across services. If span shows normal latency but metric high → metric bug.

Automated detection heuristics (to implement as monitors)
- Cardinality-drop monitor: alert if unique tag count for (model/version/route) falls by >50% over 10m vs 1h baseline.
- Duplicate-increment detector: if global counter increments faster than request receipts or trace counts by >40% sustained 5m.
- Ingestion-lag spike: queue_consumer_lag 95p > X ms AND ingestion_last_event_ts delta > 2m.
- Pipeline-error-surge: downstream aggregator write_errors/sec > threshold for 1m.
- Metric-sparsity-flood: sudden creation of >N new series in short window (possible tag explosion due to bad tagging)

Metric healing patterns (manual + automated)
- Automated temporary fallback (safety shutter):
  - If metric aggregator signals >50% error rate, route dashboards/alerts to synthetic-probe-derived SLIs. (Automated switch with 15m cooloff and manual ack).
- Auto-tag-rehydration workaround:
  - If tagging drop detected, trigger a short-lived sampling increase for traces (to capture context) and launch a sidecar job that re-aggregates raw events with best-effort tag mapping backfill.
- Duplicate-suppression:
  - Implement idempotency keys at ingestion boundary. If duplicate window detected, apply dedupe heuristic (drop duplicates based on series id + timestamp fuzz).
- Alert override & quarantine:
  - Create a quarantine label for alerts suspected to be metric corruption; suppress pager and create an incident ticket assigned to telemetry owners.

Dashboard guidance for recovery view (what to show)
- Top banner: incident verdict (user impact: YES/NO/UNKNOWN), likely mode (ingestion/tagging/agg), owners assigned.
- Comparison panes (left->right): raw-event counts, derived SLI, per-tenant slices, synthetic probes.
- For each critical SLI show: p50/p90/p99, request count, trace-sampled rate, last-write-ts.
- Attach trace snippets for five representative requests (if traces present) with latency vs SLI overlay.

Runbook snippets (copyable)
- Cardinality quick query (PromQL-like pseudo):
  - count(count_over_time(metric_name{env="prod"}[1h])) by (model)
- Duplicate detection heuristic (SQL-ish):
  - select series_id, count(*) as recs, min(ts), max(ts) from ingested_metrics where name='token_count' and ts > now()-10m group by series_id having recs > 1
- Ingestion-lag probe: check kafka_consumer_lag{consumer="metrics-aggregator"} > 1000

Post-incident recovery checklist
- Root cause note in ticket (attach dashboard snapshots and offending deploy/PR).
- If metric rename / schema change caused issue: publish migration notes and add compatibility shim for 2 weeks.
- Add automated test: metric-cardinality-regression test in CI (fail if cardinality jump/drop > 2x).
- Create a postmortem action to add a monitor (if missing) and update escalation paths.

Open questions and TODOs
- Which team owns the compatibility shim for metric renames? (observability or serving-runtime?) - TODO assigned Diego.
- Define safe thresholds for duplicate detector per-metric: currently hand-tuned for token_count only. Need corpus across models.
- Proof-of-concept: implement temporary dashboard routing to synthetic-probes during aggregator outages.

Notes to self / operator tips
- When in doubt, always check synthetic probe dashboards early — they’re the most reliable low-noise signal.
- Keep a git diff of recent metric-telemetry changes handy in oncall binder.
- Be conservative with automated healing — prefer quarantine & rapid human-in-the-loop for the first few incidents.

References and useful links
- Confluence: Observability Telemetry Cookbook (CONFLUENCE-OBS-1234)
- Jira epic: JIRA-OBS-876 (Metric reliability improvements)
- Slack thread: #obs-telemetry (search "cardinality-drop")

Appendix: quick templates
- Incident banner text (copy):
  - "[OBS] Likely metric ingestion anomaly impacting token_count SLI. No confirmed user impact. Quarantined alerts; telemetry owners paged."
- Pager message (if user impact confirmed):
  - "[URGENT] User-impacting p99 latency regression on model X since 08:13 UTC. Pager -> oncall-ops. Attach reproduction and recent deploys."

Change log
- 2025-11-02: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-12-10: added auto-detection heuristics (Priya)
- 2026-01-15: added healing patterns and runbook snippets (Diego)

Unresolved: add concrete PromQL/SQL equivalents and link code PRs once implemented.

End of cheatsheet
